open_findings.finding: src/content/legal/*/privacy.js section 5 describes Resend, Inc. as the provider of 'transactional email delivery'. In the code, merchant-facing email (welcome, newsletter, collective) is sent through Base44's Core.SendEmail integration, while Resend is called from commercialSendMessage and resendInboundWebhook (outbound commercial correspondence and inbound routing). The declaration is not false but is imprecise about which flow goes where.
open_findings.action: Legal review to confirm the correct wording; the sub-processors page already describes Base44 as covering platform-delivered transactional email and Resend as email delivery plus inbound routing.

open_findings.finding: Base44's public DPA (base44.com/dpa, accessed 2026-08-16) commits to notifying security breaches 'without undue delay as required by applicable law', with no fixed hour threshold. CAMBRA's own DPA to its merchants (DPA_MAESTRO_CAMBRA_ENCARGADO_ES.md, section 9.2) commits to a maximum of 48 hours. This is a real asymmetry in the vendor chain, not a defect in CAMBRA's text.
open_findings.action: Founder to assess: (a) negotiate a fixed contractual timeline with Base44/Wix if business volume permits, or (b) operationally mitigate (own monitoring of Base44/Wix incident status, direct support contact established) while the timeline remains unfixed. Does not block production seal — it is a vendor risk-management finding, not a CAMBRA DPA requirement.
